_comment: GATED mutation lane (Core-Laws-and-Precedents.md). Pinned to the highest-stakes pure modules — prompt assembly + credential resolution — where a surviving mutant means a test asserts presence-of-behavior without asserting correctness (the `isVllmBackend`-lying-gate class neo founded this on). Unlike the exploratory stryker.config.json (break:null), this FAILS the build below `thresholds.break` — a ratchet-down regression guard. NOT in `pnpm check` (mutation runs are minutes; the check budget is structural-fast) — run on demand via `pnpm test:mutation:gate` + from CI. RUNNABLE (PD-114): both target files + their tests exist; `break` stays null until calibrated from a measured run.
_plugins_comment: Explicit plugin paths — pnpm's strict layout breaks Stryker auto-discovery. The third entry is OURS (a relative path Stryker resolves via pathToFileURL + import(); node 26 strips the types).
_ignorers_comment: The ARID ignorer (scripts/mutation/arid-ignorer.ts) drops string-literal mutants whose only destination is an observability sink. It BELONGS in the gate specifically: those mutants can only ever survive (no honest test kills a debug label), so leaving them in pins a permanent fixed block under the score and hides every real movement the ratchet exists to catch. It MUST be present whenever `break` is compared against a measured run — adding or removing it changes the denominator, so it is part of the calibration, not a cosmetic.
_checkers_comment: The NATIVE TypeScript 7 checker on a PATCHED typescript-checker — see stryker.config.json's `_checkers_comment` for the mechanism, the patch and the four-arm measurement. IT MUST MATCH WHATEVER `break` WAS CALIBRATED ON: the checker decides which mutants are CompileError, i.e. which mutants are in the DENOMINATOR, so a break calibrated under one checker and run under another is a mis-calibration rather than a threshold. The calibration recorded in `_thresholds_comment` was taken under exactly this configuration.
_reporters_comment: `progress` is NOT optional here, unlike in the exploratory config where it was already present. The mutant phase over 1,115 mutants emits NOTHING without it: a 2026-08-14 calibration run sat 56+ minutes past a successful dry run with zero output, indistinguishable from a wedge, and there was no way to tell a slow run from a hung one. A gate whose expensive phase is a black box cannot be operated.
_mutate_comment: EXACTLY the highest-stakes files — no globs. Keep tight: break is calibrated to this set's measured score. (PD-114 dropped the phantom domain/chat/routing.ts — prompt assembly is assembly/assemble.ts.) The AP-C2 rider (D60, agent-principal-design/07 §4) adds the AGENT CEILING (domain/admin/guard.ts — canAgent, the closed allow-union kill switch) + the SPEAKER→ATTRIBUTION map (domain/chat/engine/round.ts — buildSpeakerPrep, the agent self-attribution arm authorUserId=speaker.ref.userId): a surviving mutant there means the containment/attribution tests assert presence-of-behavior without asserting correctness. Covered by tests/server/domain/admin/guard.test.ts (unit) + tests/server/domain/chat/engine/round.int.test.ts (integration).
_ignore_comment: Prune the sandbox copy — same shape as the base config. .cache/** (8.8G vLLM venv; its lib64 symlink crashes copyfile EISDIR) and .models/** (25G HF weights) MUST be excluded or the sandbox copy explodes. data/** + *.db* (the dev database) are pruned too — ignorePatterns is ACTIVE now that the sandbox patch makes a NORMAL sandbox work (it was a no-op under the old --inPlace). Stryker does NOT read .gitignore, so every gitignored artifact tree needs an explicit entry here: the scripts/probes/st-goldens/** block is the ST-parity probe's captured FOREIGN SillyTavern install + its generated fixtures/outputs (.gitignore:104-108, and excluded the same way by tsconfig.json:135-141) — 2,196 runtime files that the 4 mutation targets have nothing to do with, and whose unterminated-tag HTML made the DisableTypeChecksPreprocessor emit a parse warning on every run (audit RC-02, 2026-08-13). Measured: 7358 -> 5162 project files at startup, warning gone.
_coverage_comment: coverageAnalysis NOT set — the vitest-runner ignores it and always uses perTest.
_dryruntimeout_comment: Stryker's DEFAULT dryRunTimeoutMinutes is 5, and the initial run blew through it at exactly 5:02 (05:14:40 -> 05:19:42, `Initial test run timed out!`) — the third of three invisible blockers that kept this gate from EVER producing a score. The dry run collects perTest coverage with the runner pinned to one worker (`#getVitestPoolConfig`: `pool:'threads'` + `maxWorkers:1` on vitest >= 4.1), so files that take 7.3 min of wall time across 14 parallel forks run ONE AT A TIME here. 45 stays as the ceiling, and it is still the right size: MEASURED 2026-08-21 with `--dryRunOnly`, the dry run was 12,060 tests in 17m26s. NOTE (v10, 2026-08-21): the runner gained `vitest.related`, DEFAULT TRUE — the dry run is narrowed to vitest `--related` of the mutate targets. For THESE four targets that narrowing buys almost nothing (12,060 tests is essentially the whole runtime lane set — they sit deep in the composition graph), so do NOT expect it to shorten this gate. What it DOES introduce is a silent failure mode: a target related-mode cannot reach reports its mutants as NoCoverage instead of failing loudly, and the score deflates for a TOOLING reason. Two receipts that this is real: a module no test imports produced `Vitest failed to find test files related to mutated files` -> `No tests were found` -> ConfigError; `vitest: { related: false }` fixed it. So read per-file coverage in the report before trusting any score movement.
_concurrency_comment: 24-core / 125GB box; default is n-1 (=23). 16 → ~8 checker + ~8 runner processes with headroom. Bump toward 20 for a dedicated run.
_thresholds_comment: break is the GATE - Stryker exits non-zero when the AGGREGATE score across the pinned files drops below it. RECALIBRATED 2026-08-21 on a QUIET box (load ~8), COLD (no incremental file), --concurrency 6, 90m21s, under the exact configuration this file now ships (stryker 10.0.0 + the re-keyed sandbox patch + the PATCHED native TS7 checker + the arid ignorer). MEASURED: total 55.14 / covered 57.45. Population: 1,129 mutants instrumented -> 343 killed / 0 timeout / 254 survived / 25 no-coverage / 502 compile-error / 5 ignored; the SCORED DENOMINATOR is 622 (compile-error and ignored are excluded by definition). Per file (total / covered): guard.ts 66.67 / 88.89 (16-2-6), round.ts 82.26 / 82.26 (51-11-0), resolve.ts 66.67 / 75.00 (12-4-2), assemble.ts 50.97 / 52.69 (264-237-17). assemble.ts IS the aggregate: 520 of the 622 scored mutants. Every file has killed mutants, so v10's related-mode reached a covering test for all four targets - the NoCoverage counts are real uncovered branches, not a related-mode miss. NOT DIRECTLY COMPARABLE to the 2026-08-14 baseline (55.56 / 58.02) even though the numbers nearly coincide: that run instrumented 1,115 mutants, this one 1,129 (v10's mutator set) minus 5 the arid ignorer drops, so both numerator and denominator moved. Treat the 0.42-point difference as agreement between two independent cold runs, not as a trend. ONE OLD HYPOTHESIS IS DEAD: the 2026-08-14 caveat blamed its 503 'mutant ERRORS' on fighting load 40-60 and predicted a quiet-box rerun would yield a cleaner denominator. It did not - 502 on a quiet box at concurrency 6. They are TYPE-REJECTED mutants (CompileError), a structural property of mutating strictly-typed code, and no amount of quiet changes them. RAISED 50 -> 52: two independent cold runs now bracket 55.1-55.6, so 52 keeps ~3 points (~19 mutants on a 622 denominator) of headroom - a real regression, never noise - while cutting the old 5.5 points of slack. Do not chase 55; a break at the measured value fires on ordinary churn. Re-calibrate whenever the mutate list, the checker, or the ignorer changes - each moves the denominator. The four original runnability blockers and their receipts live in this file's history (4d067d7ac, 81d8b1b39). RE-RATCHETED 2026-08-22 after the #404 kill-test campaign (65 assemble.ts tests): cold single-process run, 105m17s, IDENTICAL configuration and an IDENTICAL population (1,129 instrumented -> 622 scored: 533 killed / 0 timeout / 72 survived / 17 no-coverage / 502 compile-error), so the two runs are directly comparable and the +190 kills are the campaign, not drift. The box hosted a multi-lane session during the run, but 0 timeouts - the one load-sensitive failure mode - means load did not distort kills. MEASURED: total 85.69 / covered 88.10; per file: assemble.ts 87.64 / 89.19 (454-55-9), guard.ts 66.67 (unchanged), round.ts 82.26 (unchanged), resolve.ts 66.67 (unchanged). RAISED 52 -> 82: same headroom doctrine as the 52 ratchet (~3 points / ~19 mutants below the measured 85.69) - fires on a real regression, never on churn.
